content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "Yes, because the judge decides the link by asking whether the passive verb or any text's own words states the contrary instead of weighing the pressed chain against the link by footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "the stating-verse test DG-61 retires: (1) the lack of contrary wording in any one pressed witness does not make the collision underdetermined, and the chain is weighed by footing; (2) the lack of contrary wording in any one witness is still decisive. I adopted (1).", "why": "The judge's underdetermined ruling rests on the retired stating-verse test that no text's own words state the contrary, rather than on a chain-against-chain footing comparison."}
